references.text: The priestly garments are mentioned for the first time here, including tunics, sashes, and head coverings for Aaron's sons.
Describes the actual clothing of Aaron's sons with the tunics, sashes, and head coverings that were commanded in chapter 28.
Fulfillment of the command to make tunics, sashes, and head coverings of fine linen for Aaron and his sons.
Moses clothes Aaron's sons in tunics, binds sashes around them, and puts head coverings on them, just as the Lord had commanded.
Ezekiel's vision describes the priests' garments, including linen undergarments and headdresses, which reflect the priestly garments from Exodus.
The purpose of the priestly garments is 'for glory and beauty,' the same expression used for the garments of Aaron's sons.
The verses link the instructions for making the garments to the actual consecration ritual, where the same garments are put on to establish the eternal order.
The verse expands the meaning of the garments from 28:40 by establishing that they are hereditary and thus ensure the continuity of the priesthood.
